issues.description: Class field identifier naming mismatch in de.tum.cit.ase.Lecture: the problem statement UML and the solution's constructor and methods use camelCase field names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), while the solution's field declarations use snake_case identifiers (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors). This causes references like this.lectureName in the constructor and methods to not match any declared field, producing a compilation error and confusing students who expect the UML camelCase names.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the field identifiers in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java consistent with the UML and the rest of the code. Rename the declared fields to camelCase: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors — or alternatively update all constructor and method references to use the snake_case names. Prefer matching the UML/camelCase variant so the class compiles and matches the problem specification.

issues.description: The exercise concept is the Lecture attributes: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors (as shown in the UML and described in the problem). In the solution implementation the fields are declared with snake_case identifiers (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) but the constructor and all getters/setters/methods use camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). This mismatch between declared field names and used identifiers prevents the code from compiling and forces students to mentally reconcile two different naming schemes for the exact same conceptual attributes, blocking straightforward mapping from UML/problem text to code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier names consistent. Rename the solution's field declarations to camelCase to match the UML and the rest of the solution: change lecture_name -> lectureName, number_of_inscribed_students -> numberOfInscribedStudents, number_of_guest_students -> numberOfGuestStudents, number_of_lecturers -> numberOfLecturers, number_of_tutors -> numberOfTutors. Alternatively, update all uses to the declared snake_case names, but preferably align template, UML and solution to camelCase so students can map the UML directly to the code.
